name: Willowherb (Epilobium)
short: Rats injected with a related species (E. hirsutum): lower drug-metabolising enzymes. 6-month trial of E. angustifolium, 128 men with enlarged prostate: no related adverse effects or liver/kidney harm.
text: Human safety data are limited: a 2018 review of Epilobium species found mostly preclinical studies and said randomized controlled trials evaluating safety and efficacy are still needed. In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 128 men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (70 given the extract, 58 placebo), capsules of a characterised Epilobium angustifolium extract taken by mouth for 6 months produced no reported adverse effects related to the extract and showed no liver or kidney toxicity. For interactions, the only data found were from an animal study of a related species, Epilobium hirsutum: in rats injected intraperitoneally with a water extract (or its constituent ellagic acid) for 9 days, the activity and levels of several liver drug-metabolising enzymes (CYP2B, CYP2C, CYP2D and CYP3A) fell, and the authors suggested this might slow drug clearance and lead to drug toxicity in people using the herb; this has not been shown in humans in the cited sources.
